🌌 Elon Musk on the future of AI compute:
“It’s always sunny in space. My prediction is that far the cheapest place to put AI will be space in 36 months or less.
It’s harder to scale on ground than it is to scale in space. Also you’re going to get about five times the effectiveness of solar panels in space versus the ground, and you don’t need batteries. It’s also much cheaper in space.
I almost wore my other shirt, which says It’s always sunny in space, which it is so because you don’t have a day night cycle or seasonality clouds or an atmosphere in space, because the atmosphere alone, results are about a 30% loss of energy.”
Endless solar power, no batteries, massive scale — AI’s next frontier could be orbit. 🚀

🌍☀️ Elon Musk on the true scale of energy:

"The Earth only receives about half a billionth of the Sun’s energy.  

The Sun is 99.8% of all mass in the solar system… Earth is in the miscellaneous category.  

Earth is like a tiny dust mote in a vast darkness.  

The way to actually scale civilization is to scale power in space."

Mind officially blown.  

We’re not energy-limited — we’re location-limited. Time to build in space. 🚀🔋

🚨 FSD Supervised 14.3 test drive with @SjvTesla!
We took the Cybertruck on a real errand loop: elementary school → Home Depot → back to the school parking lot

Zero interventions. Zero disengagements. The 20% faster reaction time (from the full AI compiler/runtime rewrite with MLIR) felt very noticeable — way more natural and decisive. 

The upgraded Reinforcement Learning stage really shines in everyday driving scenarios.
Release notes also called out “increased decisiveness of parking spot selection and maneuvering”… well, parking at the end was still a bit meh 😂

Still, this version feels like a serious step forward. Tesla AI is cooking 🔥
